scope: Connect U401.3 to U402.10; R407 translation and R1704 rotation; exact local HEAD_TX/HEAD_BUS/DISARMED/OV/INA+/ACT_UV_N/power/ground restoration. Independent development candidate only.
route: U401-2Y total 32.30809450078489 mm centerline, five through vias, 0.20 mm signal traces. End pins escape outward on B.Cu. placement_comparison: R407 shifted (-0.25,+0.60) mm at 90 degrees. R1704 retained center and rotated 180 to 270 degrees, preserving actual pin numbering. R406 90-degree trial caused reference gaps and was rejected; R406 is unchanged. Fixed connectors, MCU interfaces, outline and holes unchanged.

mounted_face_exception.reason: The fixed connector pin is inside its nominal Fab outline. Its own outward north escape must traverse a short portion of that outline before turning. This is a local package escape exception, not a route through another component. All native keepouts remain enforced.
mounted_face_exception.measurement_scope: Union of native trace strokes outside same-net pad lands against nominal Fab outlines. Not actual installed-body measurements.

Mounted on B.Cu, these parts are opposite the new F.Cu signal runs. In1 is continuous outside explicit transfer voids. No converter switch node or inductor body is in this changed region. Crosstalk and transient functional qualification remain open.

Each internal projection retains In4 reference; the F-side resistor/connector projections are also separated by the existing stack. Four dual-reference transitions pass the project stitch-distance screen. This does not establish controlled impedance, EMC immunity or physical thermal performance.

reference: No retained trace loses reference copper and no new reference gap remains. HEAD_TX and the U401-side B/In3 transfer share In4, so the dual-reference stitch screen is not applicable to those transfers. Four other new/reassigned transfers have ground distances 0.806226 to 1.932938 mm. Two new GND vias support the transitions. Six inherited flags remain; 2 mm is a project screening heuristic, not an IPC/EMC limit.
